newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Atty probes First Union loans - source.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Atty probes First Union loans - source.

text.p: The U.S. Attorneys office in Newark is investigating the conduct of First Union Bank, a unit of First Union Corp, in its attempts to sell about $14 million of non-performing loans in New Jersey, a source subpoenaed by the Grand Jury in the case told Reuters.

An official at Ramko Rolland Realty, retained by First Fidelity Bancorp as a consultant to provide brokerage and marketing services on the loan sale, said prosecutors are investigating whether or not First Fidelity, which was later acquired by First Union, made misleading statements in delivering financial statements tied to the loans.
Although Marine Midland Bank was considering buying the loans, the deal never went through, the Ramko source said.
First Union officials said they had no comment about the matter.

A subpoena dated November 1996 and obtained by Reuters said the Grand Jury wanted to see "all documents reflecting, or relating to any consulting work performed for First Union Bank in connection with the sale or other disposition of First Union Bank loans during the period from August 1995 to date."
A spokesman for the U.S. Attorneys Office in Newark said the agency can never confirm or deny the existence of an investigation.
